name: Max Area of Island
title: 1. Max Area of Island (LC 695)
why: Same flood-fill as Islands, but return the maximum component size instead of counting components.
bullets: Identical traversal to Number of Islands.
DFS returns area of current cell plus all connected land.
Track global maximum across all components.
Mark visited by setting cells to 0.

name: Number of Provinces
title: 2. Number of Provinces (LC 547)
why: Adjacency matrix graph; each unvisited node starts a new connected component (province).
bullets: Graph is implicit in the adjacency matrix.
DFS from each unvisited city floods the entire province.
Count how many times you need to start a new DFS.
Union-Find is an alternative with nearly same complexity.

name: Flood Fill
title: 3. Flood Fill (LC 733)
why: Single-source DFS/BFS flood from a starting pixel, recoloring connected same-color cells.
bullets: Classic paint-bucket: only flood cells matching original color.
Early return if new color equals original (no-op).
Same 4-directional DFS as island problems.
BFS with a queue works identically.

name: Surrounded Regions
title: 4. Surrounded Regions (LC 130)
why: Reverse thinking — DFS from border 'O's to mark safe regions; flip everything else.
bullets: Regions touching the border can never be captured.
Mark border-connected 'O's as 'S' (safe) via DFS.
Remaining 'O's are surrounded → flip to 'X'.
Restore safe cells back to 'O'.

name: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
title: 5. Pacific Atlantic Water Flow (LC 417)
why: Reverse DFS/BFS from ocean borders; cells reachable from both oceans are the answer.
bullets: Water flows uphill in reverse: from ocean inward to higher/equal cells.
Run DFS from Pacific borders and Atlantic borders separately.
Intersection of both reachable sets is the answer.
Avoids TLE from checking every cell forward to both oceans.

name: 01 Matrix
title: 6. 01 Matrix (LC 542)
why: Multi-source BFS from all 0-cells simultaneously to compute distance to nearest zero.
bullets: Seed BFS with every zero cell at distance 0.
Identical multi-source pattern to Rotting Oranges.
Relax distances as BFS expands outward.
Time O(m·n), each cell enqueued at most once per improvement.

name: Walls and Gates
title: 7. Walls and Gates (LC 286)
why: Multi-source BFS from all gates (-1) to fill empty rooms (INF) with distance to nearest gate.
bullets: Gates are BFS sources at distance 0.
Skip walls (-1) and already-filled rooms.
Mutate grid in-place with distances.
Same orange-spread template with multiple starting points.

name: Shortest Bridge
title: 8. Shortest Bridge (LC 934)
why: DFS to find first island, then multi-source BFS from its border to reach the second island.
bullets: Phase 1: DFS marks entire first island as 2 and seeds the queue.
Phase 2: BFS expands from island border into water (0-cells).
First time you hit a 1-cell (second island), return step count.
Combines island flood-fill with multi-source BFS.

name: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
title: 9. Shortest Path in Binary Matrix (LC 1091)
why: BFS shortest path on a grid with 8-directional moves; classic unweighted graph search.
bullets: BFS guarantees shortest path in unweighted grid.
8 directions including diagonals.
Mark visited by flipping 0 → 1.
Level-by-level counting gives path length.

name: Word Search
title: 10. Word Search (LC 79)
why: DFS backtracking on a grid to find a path spelling the target word.
bullets: Try DFS from every cell as a potential start.
Mark visited with '#' to prevent reuse in same path.
Backtrack by restoring character after exploring.
Prune when character mismatch or out of bounds.

name: Open the Lock
title: 11. Open the Lock (LC 752)
why: BFS on implicit state graph where each dial turn is an edge; shortest path to target.
bullets: Each lock combination is a node; 8 neighbors (4 wheels × 2 directions).
BFS finds minimum moves to target.
Deadends are blocked nodes — skip them.
Modulo arithmetic handles wrap-around (9→0, 0→9).

name: Minimum Knight Moves
title: 12. Minimum Knight Moves (LC 1197)
why: BFS on an infinite chessboard; each knight jump is one unweighted edge.
bullets: Symmetry: work in first quadrant via absolute values.
BFS from (0,0) outward guarantees minimum moves.
8 fixed knight move offsets.
Allow nr/nc ≥ -1 to handle negative quadrants correctly.

name: Keys and Rooms
title: 13. Keys and Rooms (LC 841)
why: DFS/BFS graph traversal from room 0; visit all reachable nodes.
bullets: Rooms form a directed graph; keys are edges.
DFS from room 0 collects all reachable rooms.
Return true iff every room was visited.
BFS with a queue is equally valid.

name: Course Schedule
title: 14. Course Schedule (LC 207)
why: Cycle detection in a directed graph via DFS or Kahn's BFS topological sort.
bullets: Build adjacency list and indegree array from prerequisites.
Kahn's algorithm: BFS courses with indegree 0.
Decrement indegree when a prerequisite is satisfied.
Cycle exists iff taken < numCourses (not all courses reachable).

name: Clone Graph
title: 15. Clone Graph (LC 133)
why: BFS/DFS traversal with a HashMap to clone each node and its neighbors.
bullets: BFS visits all nodes reachable from the start.
HashMap maps original node → cloned node.
Create clone on first discovery; wire neighbors via map lookup.
DFS with same map pattern is equally common in interviews.

name: Swim in Rising Water
title: 16. Swim in Rising Water (LC 778)
why: Binary search on answer time T, then BFS to check if path exists using only cells with height ≤ T.
bullets: Answer is the minimum time T when a path from top-left to bottom-right exists.
Binary search T in [max(start,end), n²-1].
For each T, BFS checks reachability using cells with height ≤ T.
Dijkstra is an alternative but binary search + BFS is simpler to explain.
Time O(n² log n²) with BFS O(n²) per check.
